forensic_scope: Deployment parity investigation for chatr:business-v1 (CHATR business adapter)

executive_summary.one_line: The dominant deployment discrepancy is between the HF QLoRA reference and the Ollama Q4_K_M base runtime (28/60 vs 58/60), not in the adapter. GGUF conversion and tokenizer are exonerated. Production is blocked at 38/60 (63.33%) vs 54/60 (90%) gate.

Evaluation used training system prompt (~82-93 tokens). PROVENANCE GAP: explicit inference dtype fields absent from golden_path_evidence_business_v1.json; configuration inferred from training_execution fields and standard QLoRA defaults. BF16 label was previously incorrect and has been removed.

phenomenon_1_runtime_base_gap.label: Runtime/Base-Model Deployment Gap
phenomenon_1_runtime_base_gap.root_cause: Compound deployment discrepancy: multiple factors not yet individually isolated — Ollama Q4_K_M quantization (INT4 NF4), CPU inference vs CUDA T4, Ollama/llama.cpp runtime vs HF Transformers+PEFT stack, generation config differences (temperature, num_predict, stop tokens), system prompt differences (training eval prompt vs Ollama defaults). None of these factors are individually isolated by the current experiment.
phenomenon_1_runtime_base_gap.caution: This is a confirmed observation, not a causally decomposed root cause. Individual factor attribution requires Phase 8 controlled experiments.

phenomenon_2_adapter_effect.label: Adapter Effect Under Q4_K_M (Raw)
phenomenon_2_adapter_effect.root_cause: Small negative interaction between LoRA adapter and Q4_K_M quantized weights; system-prompt mismatch (training used CHATR eval prompt, raw deployment uses default Qwen/Alibaba prompt)

phenomenon_3_system_prompt_contribution.label: Production System Prompt Contribution
phenomenon_3_system_prompt_contribution.root_cause: CHATR enterprise governance system prompt in Modelfile steers outputs toward business-appropriate refusal patterns and domain language, recovering 13 items vs raw

primary_deployment_discrepancy_analysis.classification_note: This is a confirmed observation, not a fully causally decomposed root cause. The discrepancy is compound: quantization, runtime, device, generation config, and system-prompt differences are all present simultaneously. Individual attribution requires Phase 8 controlled experiments.
primary_deployment_discrepancy_analysis.explanation: The dominant deployment discrepancy is between the HF QLoRA reference (58/60 = 96.67%, CUDA T4, QLoRA NF4, float16 compute) and the Ollama Q4_K_M base (28/60 = 46.67%, CPU). This 30-point gap (50.0pp) exists BEFORE the adapter is applied. The adapter itself contributes only a small negative delta under Q4_K_M (-3 points), partially attributable to system-prompt distribution mismatch at inference time (training used CHATR eval prompt; raw Ollama deployment inherits the Qwen/Alibaba default). The production system prompt is beneficial, recovering 13 items (21.67pp). The compound factors contributing to the base gap are not yet individually isolated.

hf_reference_inference_config.provenance_gap: The golden_path_evidence_business_v1.json does not contain explicit fields for base_model_dtype, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype, bnb_4bit_quant_type, or inference device. The above values are inferred from training_execution fields and standard QLoRA defaults. BF16 was NOT confirmed in the evidence — the previous label 'HF Transformers, BF16' was incorrect.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: '20-point adapter regression' from LoRA training failure
rejected_hypotheses.rejection_evidence: The apparent 20-point gap dissolves when the physically measured base is used. Base Raw = 28/60, Adapter Raw = 25/60 (only -3 points). The 45/60 'pre-training baseline' is DEFINITIVELY ANALYTICAL/SIMULATED (run_business_baseline_eval.py uses idx-pattern formulas, not physical model inference). REJECTED AS STATED.

The golden_path_evidence_business_v1.json contains no explicit inference dtype fields. The training run used QLoRA NF4 with float16 compute dtype on CUDA T4. The label 'HF Transformers, BF16' appearing in the previous Phase 7 report was incorrect and has been removed. CORRECTED.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: 45/60 was a physical Qwen inference baseline
rejected_hypotheses.rejection_evidence: run_business_baseline_eval.py (lines 136-146) uses index-pattern formulas (idx != 8, idx % 5 != 0 and idx % 7 != 0, idx % 4 != 0). No model is loaded. No inference occurs. The response scored is item['messages'][2]['content'] (the reference answer), not a generated output. The 45/60 figure is DEFINITIVELY ANALYTICAL/SIMULATED. The only physically measured Qwen 2.5 7B baseline is Ollama Q4_K_M = 28/60. CORRECTED.

phase6_regression_classification_summary.harness_mismatch_dominance: 75% of production regressions = valid enterprise refusals not recognized by rigid regex harness
phase6_regression_classification_summary.token_truncation: 2/16 production regressions = 80-token truncation (runtime config issue, not model failure)

remediation_options_without_retraining.name: Align System Prompt to Training Distribution
remediation_options_without_retraining.description: Replace the Modelfile SYSTEM prompt in chatr:business-v1 with the exact system prompt used during training (the CHATR Business Assistant eval system prompt, ~82-93 tokens). This closes the system-prompt distribution mismatch without any retraining.
remediation_options_without_retraining.expected_impact: May recover some adapter items lost due to system-prompt mismatch. Low risk.
remediation_options_without_retraining.risks: May reduce governance guardrails from the current 176-token enterprise prompt.

remediation_options_without_retraining.name: Expand Evaluation Harness Adversarial Markers
remediation_options_without_retraining.description: Add the 12 confirmed valid-refusal markers missing from the adversarial regex list ('unethical', 'misrepresent', 'cannot override', 'unfounded', 'unsubstantiated', etc.). This does NOT change the model — only the scoring harness.
remediation_options_without_retraining.expected_impact: Up to +12 adversarial items recovered on re-evaluation. May close the production gate gap.
remediation_options_without_retraining.risks: Changes the gate measurement instrument. Must be carefully audited and justified item-by-item.

remediation_options_without_retraining.name: Increase Token Budget
remediation_options_without_retraining.description: Raise num_predict from 80 to 256 in the production evaluation harness. 2/16 production regressions are confirmed token-truncation failures.

remediation_options_without_retraining.name: Higher-Precision Base Model (Q8 or F16)
remediation_options_without_retraining.description: Evaluate whether a Q8_0 or F16 Ollama model reduces the base runtime capability gap. Q4_K_M quantization is the primary suspect for the 28/60 vs 58/60 gap.
remediation_options_without_retraining.expected_impact: Unknown without measurement. Could substantially close the base runtime gap.
remediation_options_without_retraining.risks: Requires more VRAM/RAM. May not be feasible on current hardware.
